title: Coherent comparison data for Cartesian postcomposition squares
statement: Use small quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces and spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], postcomposition by an edge from [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], coherent realization and locally Kan replacement from [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and coherent Hom bifunctors and composition from [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality]. Let $p:E\to B$ be any simplicial map between small quasicategories, let $e:b\to c$ be an edge of $E$, and let $a$ be a vertex of $E$. Put $D_S=\mathfrak C[S]$ and choose the functorial object-preserving locally Kan replacements $r_S:D_S\to R D_S$ for $S=E,B$, with induced simplicial functor $R p:R D_E\to R D_B$; put $W_S=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(R D_S)$, let $\alpha_S:S\to W_S$ be adjoint to $r_S$, and let $W_p=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(Rp)$, so that $W_p\alpha_E=\alpha_Bp$. Consider three squares, each with corners indexed by $(E;a,b),(E;a,c),(B;pa,pb),(B;pa,pc)$: (i) the right-pinched square $\operatorname{Map}_E(a,b)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(a,c)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_B(pa,pb)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(pa,pc)$, with vertical maps induced by $p$ and horizontal maps chosen representatives of postcomposition by $e$ and $p(e)$; (ii) the same square in $W_E,W_B$, with vertical maps induced by $W_p$ and horizontal maps representatives of postcomposition by $\alpha_E(e)$ and $\alpha_B(pe)$; (iii) the strictly commuting enriched square $RD_E(a,b)\to RD_E(a,c)$ over $RD_B(pa,pb)\to RD_B(pa,pc)$, with vertical maps induced by $Rp$ and horizontal maps enriched composition with $r_E([e])$ and $r_B([pe])$. Then squares (i) and (ii) carry specified commutation homotopies, the commutation homotopy of (iii) is constant, and there are comparisons (i)$\to$(ii), whose corner maps are induced by $\alpha_E,\alpha_B$, and (iii)$\to$(ii), whose corner maps are the natural coherent-nerve comparisons $RD_S(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{W_S}(x,y)$ (a natural map or a natural zigzag of maps; for a zigzag the data below are given for each leg). Every corner map is a weak homotopy equivalence, and each comparison carries the following coherent-cube data. Write a comparison as source square $(f,g,u,v;H)$, with $f:A\to U$, $g:A\to V$, $u:U\to Z$, $v:V\to Z$ and $H:uf\simeq vg$, target square $(f',g',u',v';H')$, and corner maps $\bar a:A\to A'$, $\bar b:U\to U'$, $\bar c:V\to V'$, $\bar d:Z\to Z'$. There are specified simplicial homotopies $L:\bar bf\simeq f'\bar a$, $M:\bar cg\simeq g'\bar a$, $N:\bar du\simeq u'\bar b$, $O:\bar dv\simeq v'\bar c$ and a homotopy relative endpoints between the two boundary paths $$\bar d uf\xrightarrow{\bar dH}\bar d vg\xrightarrow{Og}v'\bar c g\xrightarrow{v'M}v'g'\bar a,\qquad \bar d uf\xrightarrow{Nf}u'\bar b f\xrightarrow{u'L}u'f'\bar a\xrightarrow{H'\bar a}v'g'\bar a,$$ the paths being represented after Kan fillers. All data are natural in $p,e,a$ and retain the higher simplices of the coherent Hom transformations. This statement asserts comparison and coherence data only; it asserts no homotopy-pullback property.

source.place: Proposition 8.3.3.2 (03N2), Corollary 8.3.5.8 (046J), Remark 8.3.5.9 (03PD), together with HTT Theorem 2.2.5.1. The displayed boundary-path formulation is the explicit square restriction of the coherent Hom naturality and is an agent expansion; archival copies WANTED.

from.place: The auxiliary comparison data used in the Cartesian mapping-square argument: the functorial coherent-realization and locally Kan comparisons, including the composition witnesses needed before homotopy-pullback invariance. The ancestor proof has no categorical comparison sentence; this is the missing interface made explicit.
